_note: Numbers are CEILINGS in bytes, not baselines: the check fails when an artifact is larger, and does nothing otherwise. Set an entry to null to measure and report it without ever failing. See scripts/check-size.mjs for why this is a ceiling rather than a baseline plus a tolerance -- briefly, a tolerance fails whenever the compiler moves and has to be re-recorded to go green, which is a tripwire moved to wherever the wire already was.
_desktopCeiling: 70 MB for the desktop binary, chosen rather than measured. It sits at ~52.6 MB with thin LTO, so there is real room for the features Milestone 3 and 4 still owe -- and 70 MB of raw binary is roughly a 21 MB installer at the ~3.4x compression the NSIS bundle achieves, which is still a reasonable thing to ask someone to download. If a change needs more than this, that is a conversation, not a number to nudge.
_cliCeiling: The CLI gets the same ceiling for the simple reason that it links the same Typst compiler and there is no argument for holding it to a different standard. It sits far below, around 38 MB.
_distCeiling: 4 MB for the frontend bundle against ~1.9 MB today. Deliberately not generous: the mermaid decision (see CLAUDE.md) turned on a ~2-3 MB chunk being too much to add, so a ceiling that would let mermaid in without comment would not be enforcing the decision this file exists to enforce. Note dist grew 16.2% between 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-31 -- the Tasks tenant, the help panel and the changelog reader -- and under the old baseline-plus-tolerance scheme that failed the build for a month while nobody looked at it.
_binaryNameNote: essay-cli's [[bin]] is named `essay`, not `essay-cli` (see crates/essay-cli/Cargo.toml) -- `cargo build -p essay-cli` produces target/release/essay.exe. essay-desktop has no [[bin]] override, so its binary matches the package name: target/release/essay-desktop.exe.
_platformNote: The paths are Windows-shaped because the `size` job's budget leg runs on windows-latest, which is also where the numbers above were measured. The macOS and Linux legs of that matrix exist to warm the release cache and do not run this check.
